ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm whether the 08:42–08:54 segment (F3) was actually driven on Balestier Road (check the driven path / road names behind F3); if it was not, apply the RD-2 mileage refund of $6.68 as a voucher.
ruling.reasoning: The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride: the fare fact breaks the $40.45 charged into base $3.90, distance $26.80 (19.01 km), time $8.17 (31.4 min), waiting $0.11 and platform $1.47, with no surge (1.0×) [F7][F6], so extra distance enters the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch (not FARE-1) governs [F4][RD-2]. The GPS record establishes one off-route segment, 08:42–08:54, 7.24 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.50 km, +4.74 km extra and up to 1568 m from the optimal route, on a trip that ran 19.0 km against 13.9 km optimal (+5.1 km, +37%) [F3][F1][RD-1], and it is not excused by traffic: there is no incident fact near the route during the trip window, and a speed-band reading alone is only corroboration under RD-4(b) [F15][F12][RD-4]. The decisive question is the scope of the rider's agreement: at 08:39 the driver asked "ok if I go round via Balestier Road?" and at 08:40 the rider replied "可以，走 Balestier Road 吧。", one minute before the segment began [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. That is an agreement to a specifically named road, so under RD-5 it covers driving on Balestier Road only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road [F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the record does: the segment fact gives only distance and elapsed time and names no street [F3], no chat message places the car on Balestier Road [F8][F9][F10], and the driver's own post-trip statement is not rider consent and adds no road tie [F11][RD-5][G11]. Both advocates read this ground identically as named_road_untied, and the trace carries no road names for the driven path, so the reading is undetermined rather than settled [F3][F9][RD-5]. Because that finding changes the amount, the case cannot be decided on this record and must go to a person. The amount was computed for the record: on the off-route segment the RD-2 rate is this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, $26.80 ÷ 19.01 km = $1.4098/km [F7][F4], so 4.74 km × $1.4098/km = $6.68; the billed excess of $7.22 covers 5.12 km [F4] and the balance (~0.38 km of corridor/jitter mileage) is expressly not refundable under RD-2 [F4][F3][RD-2] — this figure applies only if the segment is found non-exempt, which is not something this record settles. No flag_account: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days and the driver's profile shows 0 [F18][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages, the driver's statement and the traffic/weather facts; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [F8][F9][F11][F16][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message sent before the segment began (08:40 vs segment start 08:42) names a specific road: '可以，走 Balestier Road 吧。' in reply to the driver's 'ok if I go round via Balestier Road?' [F8][F9][F3]. Under RD-5 a named-road agreement covers driving on that road only and the record must tie the segment to it; F3 gives only distance and time and names no street, no chat message places the car on Balestier Road, and the driver's post-trip statement is not rider consent [F3][F10][F11][RD-5][G11]. rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as to the measurement (F1, F3) but not as to consequence: RD-1 sends every off-route segment to be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and here RD-5 is undetermined, not failed [F3][RD-1][RD-5].

The named_road_untied reading is right, but the consequence is not 'counts': where nothing ties the segment to the agreed road and nothing places it elsewhere the finding is undetermined under G13, and the case goes to a person rather than the exemption failing outright [F3][F9][RD-5].

Correct that RD-4 needs an incident on the replaced stretch and F15 shows none [F15][RD-4], but RD-4 is not the only exemption route; the driver relies on the pre-segment agreement in F8/F9 [F8][F9][RD-5].
The band-2 reading (F12) does not exempt on its own under RD-4(b) [F12][RD-4], but the driver did not rest on it; it was the operational reason disclosed in F8 [F8][RD-5].

The arithmetic of $6.68 follows from RD-2's segment basis (4.74 km × $1.4098/km) [F3][F7], but $7.22 relates to the billed 5.12 km of excess distance [F4] and the ~0.38 km corridor/jitter balance is not refundable [RD-2]; more importantly the amount is not awardable here because the segment's status is undetermined and the case escalates [RD-5].
Timing alone does not make the agreement cover the segment: the agreement was to a named road and the record must tie the segment to it, which F3, F8, F9 and F10 do not [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].
F12 is a speed-band record only, which RD-4(b) accepts as corroboration and not as a standalone exemption, and F15 shows no incident on the replaced optimal stretch [F12][F15][RD-4].

There is no stop fact [F3], but the ground both sides raise is named_road_untied, and the record does not tie the 7.24 km segment replacing 2.50 km, reaching 1568 m off the optimal route, to the agreed road [F3][F1][RD-5].

The conclusion that nothing is refundable assumes the segment is exempt under RD-5, but the scope of that agreement is undetermined on this record and the finding changes the amount [F3][F9][RD-5][RD-2].
